svg.aria-label: Desk Sage's architecture: Claude Code's hooks post to the bridge on my Mac, the bridge asks Sage's mind for an act, and sends lines over USB serial, Wi-Fi, the emulator's events or QEMU's pty to the ESP32-S3, which plays Sage from its flash on the display under the prism; a tap goes back up
svg.title: Desk Sage · architecture
svg.desc: Left, my Mac: Claude Code, whose hooks post each event to the bridge on 127.0.0.1:47823; the bridge, which keeps one mood for every session and sends a heartbeat every 15 s; Sage's mind, a Node process that answers each signal with an act or nothing within 0.3 s; and sage.bin, Sage baked in headless Chrome, whose acts the mind reads. Middle, the link: USB serial at 115,200 baud through the board's CH343, Wi-Fi on TCP port 4210, the emulator's Server-Sent Events, or a pty for QEMU. Right, the device: the ESP32-S3R8 plays sage.bin from its own flash partition at 24 frames a second on the 240 by 240 display under the prism, and its motion sensor feels a tap over 0.35 g, which goes back up to the bridge. Below, the stand-ins used before the board arrives: the emulator, a web page, and QEMU running the real firmware. With no line for 60 s the board goes its own way.
svg.text: From my Mac to the desk. Ports, rates and timeouts from the code; the numbers follow the flow in the legend.
The link, one line at a time
for every session; h every 15 s
an act or nothing, in 0.3 s
so it floats in the glass
a tap: a jolt over 0.35 g
Each Claude Code event runs a small async hook: curl -s -m 1
posts its JSON to 127.0.0.1:47823, and the bridge answers 204
The bridge merges every session into one mood and reads a
command only for its kind, then tells Sage's mind just that:
tests failed, a push, Claude stopped, a tap.
The mind answers each line in order with an act or nothing
(cooldowns, priorities, never the same act twice running); no
answer in 0.3 s and the bridge carries on without it.
One line at a time over the link: s <mood> when the mood
changes, e <act> for an act, and h with the time every 15 s.
The emulator and QEMU get the same lines.
A tap on the glass goes back up as tap, and the mind decides
what it means: a hello, looking up, a knock, a dance, or a sulk
With no line for 60 s the board goes its own way: into the
rain, its antenna dark, fidgeting and answering taps itself.
The next line brings it back with a hello.
